newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan stocks fall, parallel market spooked.
newsitem.headline: Jordan stocks fall, parallel market spooked.

text.p: Shares on Jordan's main stock exchange fell 0.20 percent on Sunday after the parallel market took fright from a bout of early selling, brokers said.
The Amman Financial Market 60-share index fell 0.30 points to 147.05 points in trade worth 320,000 dinars ($452,000).
But the parallel market of newly listed shares, which trades for half an hour before the main market opens, registered across the board losses after a wave of sustained selling.
Brokers said the market was spooked by an early trade of Middle East Complex shares at 0.63 dinars -- five percent lower than Saturday's closing price.

"When the investors saw this very low price, they panicked. They thought something had happened that they not heard about," said Nasser al-Amad, general manager of United Financial Investment. "The parallel market was paralysed."
Sixteen shares fell, five of them by the five percent maximum allowed during one trading day. Turnover on the parallel market almost matched that of the main market.
Amad said calm returned before the opening of the main market. But the bourse maintained its gradual slide downwards in shallow trade.
Jordan Gulf Bank and Arab Bank Group again accounted for almost half of the day's turnover. Jordan Gulf Bank closed unchanged at 0.89 dinars and Arab Bank fell one dinar to 245 dinars.
Amad said the heavy trade in Jordan Gulf Bank was the result of a single investor offloading stock. "But there are plenty of other people ready to support it at that level," he said.

Seven stocks rose on the main market, but three biggest risers, Real Estate Investment, Middle East Hotels and Beit al-Mal mustered a combined turnover of less than 4,000 dinars. Shares in 21 stocks fell and eight traded but closed unchanged.

The AFM index has been stuck for the seven weeks within a point either side of 147.7 points. Daily turnover has halved during the same period to around 500,000 dinars from about one million dinars a day in September.
